title: Housing payment and insurance risk are unevenly distributed by income and place
source_unit: Federal Reserve Survey of Household Economics and Decisionmaking adult respondent, 2025 housing module
geography: United States; income and neighborhood-income comparisons

denominator.unit: weighted renter adult population estimate; published subgroup percentages use renter question frame

renters_below_50000_income_behind.unit: percent of renters with income below $50,000, approximate one-third

renters_at_least_100000_income_behind.unit: percent of renters with income at least $100,000

observations.method: Federal Reserve 2025 SHED published housing estimates; rent arrears refer to being behind at some point in the prior year.
observations.uncertainty: Self-reported cross-sectional estimates do not identify arrears duration, notice, eviction filing, payment source, rent burden, or later move/stay outcome.
observations.counterinterpretation: Income categories combine different rents, household sizes, savings, assistance, and local markets; arrears do not equal eviction or homelessness.

denominator.unit: weighted homeowner adult population estimate; published subgroup percentages use homeowner question frame

low_or_moderate_income_neighborhood_with.unit: percent of homeowners in low- or moderate-income neighborhoods

high_income_neighborhood_without_insuran.unit: percent of homeowners in high-income neighborhoods

income_below_50000_without_insurance.unit: percent of homeowners with income below $50,000, approximate two in ten

observations.method: Federal Reserve 2025 SHED housing and insurance estimates; neighborhood income and family income are separate conditioning variables.
observations.uncertainty: The survey does not establish policy terms, mortgage status for every case, insurer availability, hazard exposure, claim history, or whether coverage would have been adequate.
observations.subgroup: Homeowners by neighborhood income and family income.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some owners may self-insure or prefer not to buy coverage; absence of insurance is not by itself evidence of insurer withdrawal or an unmet claim.

denominator.unit: published homeowner insurance question frames; conditional shares are not mutually exclusive

uninsured_could_not_afford.unit: percent of uninsured homeowners reporting main reason

uninsured_not_worth_cost.unit: percent of uninsured homeowners reporting main reason

insured_income_below_50000_struggle_prem.unit: percent of insured homeowners with income below $50,000, approximate

observations.method: Federal Reserve 2025 SHED conditional responses about the main reason for no insurance and affordability among insured owners.
observations.uncertainty: Reported affordability is not a premium quote, coverage adequacy measure, claim outcome, or direct observation of insurer pricing or nonrenewal.
observations.subgroup: Uninsured and insured homeowners, with income-conditioned affordability comparisons.
observations.counterinterpretation: Preference for more coverage, premium struggle, and no insurance can reflect different perceived hazards, deductibles, assets, mortgage requirements, or self-insurance choices.

denominator.unit: annual SHED renter and homeowner question frames; separate year-specific cross-sectional estimates

observations.method: Matched annual Federal Reserve SHED housing report pages; the 2024 report covers survey-year 2024 and the 2025 report covers survey-year 2025. The published 2025 report also describes the rent-arrears change from 2024.
observations.uncertainty: Separate cross-sectional surveys do not track the same households; small percentage-point changes may reflect sampling or question-frame differences. The homeowner insurance question was not identical for mortgage and free-and-clear owners in the 2024 footnote.
observations.subgroup: All renters for rent arrears and all homeowners for insurance status, compared across annual report years.
observations.counterinterpretation: The comparison describes movement in reported prevalence, not a causal effect of premiums, hazards, income, eviction, insurer behavior, or policy change.

related_sources.claim: The 2025 Federal Reserve hardship report supplies related household financial and health-cost context.
related_sources.access_boundary: Separate report modules are not a longitudinal household event record.

boundary: This record establishes reported rent arrears, homeowner insurance gaps, neighborhood/income differences, and insurance affordability pressure. It does not establish causation, claim adequacy, insurer withdrawal, eviction, displacement, repair, health, debt, or political response.
